key_insight: Scal3R uses lightweight test-time training to adapt feed-forward 3D reconstruction models online, enabling accurate and consistent large-scale reconstructions from very long video sequences while keeping memory use low.
problem_solved: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models degrade on long video sequences because they have limited memory and cannot effectively capture global contextual cues, causing drift and inconsistent geometry across a large scene.
method: Perform test-time training (online adaptation) as frames arrive so the model learns scene-specific appearance and geometry cues during inference.
Use scalable streaming/memory-efficient strategies (e.g., incremental summarization or windowed optimization) to handle arbitrarily long sequences without exploding memory.
Enforce geometry- and temporal-consistency objectives to fuse local predictions into a globally coherent large-scale reconstruction.
impact: Makes deployment of learned 3D reconstruction systems practical for real-world long-form video capture (e.g., mapping, AR/VR, robotics) by improving accuracy and consistency without prohibitive memory or compute costs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: incoming video → test-time training loop → updated model → cumulative 3D mesh/volume
Before/after reconstructions: feed-forward output vs. Scal3R output on a long video showing reduced drift
Timeline/memory graphic: streaming frames with a compact scene summary highlighting constant/low memory footprint
Accuracy vs. sequence length chart: reconstruction quality decays for baseline but stays stable for Scal3R
paper_title: Scal3R: Scalable Test-Time Training for Large-Scale 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Tao Xie, Peishan Yang, Yudong Jin, Yingfeng Cai, Wei Yin
